newsitem.title: USA: Brazil needs to privatize, lower public debt - Malan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil needs to privatize, lower public debt - Malan.

text.p: Brazil Finance Minister Pedro Malan said Monday that Brazil needs to move forward on privatization and reducing public sector spending in order to build sustainable growth with low inflation.
"To consolidate the gains we've had so far, we need to push forward on privatization and reduction of the consolidated public debt," Malan said. "That's precisely what we intend to do."
Malan told reporters after speaking at a conference on Brazil here that it was "too early" to tell whether the government's operational deficit would need to be revised higher.
"We still think it's 3.0 to 3.5 percent of GDP, down from five percent last year," Malan said.
He reaffirmed the government's commitment to sell off state enterprises and said that these privatizations would also help reduce public debt.
"Privatization has taken hold and will go forward, and over time will reduce the contribution of state enterprises to the consolidated public debt," he said.
The government will continue to press the Brazilian Congress to approve reforms in the social security system and expects the Senate to discuss the measures in October, Malan said.
"We are going to insist on change in the social security system," he said.
The finance minister reaffirmed Brazil's commitment to building higher growth at the same time as it maintains a guard against inflation.
"The reduction in inflation is there to stay," Malan said.
He also said that the government's strategy of issuing domestic debt and lowering inflation was sustainable.
